lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Remove the date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They disclose personal information without strengthening most U.S. applications.

items.says: Add a city or region if you want to show where you are based.
Make sure the LinkedIn URL is clickable.
Clarify the expected completion status if the MBA was not completed in June 2025.
items.because: Recruiters may otherwise misread your current status.

items.says: Clarify whether the 35% conversion gain is relative or in percentage points.
Give the measurement period or comparison basis for the conversion gain.
Clarify whether “all merchants” describes the rollout or the conversion population.
items.because: Those are different claims.

items.says: Make sure the evidence supports attributing the full conversion change to the redesign.
items.because: The current wording makes a causal claim.

items.says: Include a post-launch result for dispute self-service if available.
items.because: The bullet stops at shipping.

items.says: If there is no post-launch result, clarify your specific contribution and the basis for “two weeks ahead.”
Specify the currency of the 1.1 million figure.
Clarify the loss period and whether the figure is estimated or observed.
Explain how the analysis informed the roadmap decision.
Clarify whether you closed the 140 tickets or coordinated a team that did.
items.because: The bullet should not overstate your individual ownership.

items.says: Add the period or starting point for the queue reduction if available.
Add what the comparison showed, if the finding is reliable.
items.because: The bullet describes a comparison but not its result.

items.says: Do not treat the opt-in comparison as proof that the redesign caused an outcome without supporting analysis.
items.because: Merchants who opted in may differ from those who stayed on the old flow.

items.says: Clarify the pilot period and how median time to first payment was measured.
Check whether this onboarding result is distinct from the one in the practicum.
items.because: The same result appears there.

items.says: “Cut late deliveries” presents a changed calculation as improved delivery performance.
items.because: Excluding weather-delayed shipments changes the metric, not necessarily delivery performance.

items.says: Add the measurement period and basis for the 30% pick-error reduction if possible.
“Coordinated” and “prepares” have mismatched tenses.
Add a concrete outcome or purpose for the forecast pack.
items.because: The bullet describes recurring responsibilities but gives little evidence of impact.

items.says: Clarify whether the 1,800 hours are annualized or measured over a full year.
Explain how the driver-hour savings were estimated.
Consider naming the route-planning tool if it is relevant to target roles.
Clarify whether 3,100 students were reached, registered, or active.
items.because: That detail helps readers assess the scale of the result.

items.says: Clarify whether two dining halls were the full launch scope.
items.because: That detail helps readers assess the scale of the result.

items.says: Show how the nine tonnes of food were tracked if available.
items.because: That detail helps readers assess the result’s credibility.

items.says: Add the time period for the increase in weekly active users.
Avoid attributing the entire user increase to reminders without supporting evidence.
Clarify the measurement period for the volunteer-shift results.
Explain how staff cover shifts were counted.
Say what the working sessions enabled or changed.
items.because: The bullet describes an activity, not its outcome.

items.says: Clarify the work’s scope if “across the network” is broader than the clinics involved.
Make your contribution to the intake changes clearer.
items.because: The passive construction obscures your role.

items.says: Quantify how much the intake form was shortened.
items.because: “Shortened” does not say how much changed.

items.says: Clarify the adoption or outcome of the intake changes.
items.because: The bullet does not say what improved.

items.says: The first-payment result appears to duplicate the Harbor Payments onboarding result.
items.because: It repeats the 2,300-merchants figure.

items.says: The merchant first-payment result does not fit the hospital practicum.
Make the broad product-skills list more specific to skills you can discuss.
Consider adding relevant tools you can explain using.
items.because: The tools list is short.

items.says: Use consistent capitalization and category formatting in the Skills section.
items.because: It improves readability and helps recruiters scan the section.
